sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Imogen Foulkes
articles.description: Switzerland's glaciers are disappearing at a record pace. More than 5% of their ice has vanished this year alone — threatening water supplies, ecosystems and communities across Europe.
articles.title: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss

articles.author: Quil Lawrence
articles.description: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth told hundreds of junior military officers and enlisted leaders on Wednesday that the Trump administration has achieved a cultural shift in the military.
articles.title: Leaning into culture war flashpoints, Hegseth says he has transformed U.S. military

articles.author: Emily Feng
articles.description: As a Syrian glassmaker created his wares in Damascus, watching his craft reminded this reporter to slow down and enjoy the moment.
articles.title: Greetings from Syria, where time seems to melt as a glassmaker braves scorching temps

articles.author: Jaclyn Diaz
articles.description: The Cornell lawsuit filed by a woman alleging a brutal rape raises questions on how police handle such cases. The majority of police lack adequate training on trauma-informed approaches, experts say.
articles.title: Police questioning can shape a sexual assault case. Their approach is often wrong

articles.author: Hansi Lo Wang
articles.description: The Pentagon made last-minute changes to forms that many overseas U.S. citizens use for absentee voting, removing a category of citizens that Republicans have been pushing to block from voting.
articles.title: Trump officials changed forms for overseas voters amid a GOP push to restrict voting

articles.author: Danielle Kurtzleben
articles.description: The Trump administration has taken government equity stakes in more than three dozen private companies.
articles.title: How Trump keeps undercutting his anti-communist message

articles.author: Catherine Sweeney
articles.description: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, no matter the method.
articles.title: After failed execution, health workers say Tennessee's method flouts medical ethics

articles.author: Kat Lonsdorf
articles.description: As the plane went into a spin and began to plunge, passengers and crew members got into the cockpit, subdued the pilot and diverted the flight to land in Saudi Arabia, Israel's leader says.
articles.title: On flight to Israel, pilot is stabbed, plane plunges before passengers tackle attacker

articles.author: Jenna McLaughlin
articles.description: The FBI says it's addressing a massive data breach, vowing to go after the hackers it believes are responsible.
articles.title: FBI hunting the hackers who stole its employees' sensitive data

articles.author: Geoff Brumfiel
articles.description: Valar Atomics wants to place over 450 reactors on more than 9,500 acres in Utah to power a huge data center project.
articles.title: A startup wants to build a massive nuclear-powered data center on public land in Utah

articles.author: Achol Arok (now) and Nick Visser (earlier)
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Queensland’s state government has missed a deadline to sign up to the federal government’s Thriving Kids program before its rollout begins today.
Under the program, state governments will provide supports to children up to 8 years old with mild to moderate autism or developmental delays. They will be made ineligible for federal aid through the NDIS in 2028.
This scheme is helping Australians, particularly young Australians, get their foot in the door and achieve the dream of home ownership. When it comes to housing challenges, we’re tackling it from every angle – making it easier for first home buyers, boosting supply and helping renters get a better deal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: Anika Wells named in Time’s ‘influential rising stars’; NSW seeks to join Queensland in ‘from the river to the sea’ ban case

articles.author: Tess Ikonomou
articles.description:
Israeli embassy says the Sydney couple were on board flight that was dramatically diverted after one pilot allegedly stabbed the other
Two Australian citizens were onboard a flight to Tel Aviv that was diverted after one of the pilots allegedly stabbed the other in an attack, according to the Israeli embassy.
The passengers are a Jewish couple from Sydney, the embassy in Australia confirmed to the Guardian on Thursday. No further details were provided.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australian couple among passengers on diverted flydubai flight to Israel, embassy says

articles.author: Heather Stewart, Richard Partington and Jillian Ambrose
articles.description:
Millions of people in Great Britain face increase from Thursday to an average of £1,723 a year for a typical home
John Healey is under growing pressure to offer fresh energy support for households in next month’s budget as millions face a 4% rise in charges from Thursday to an average of £1,723 a year for a typical home.
In his speech at Labour’s conference in Liverpool this week, the chancellor warned that the government had limited resources to cushion the worldwide economic shocks hitting Britain, while arguing his budget would have fiscal discipline at its core.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healey urged to offer energy support in budget as bills rise 4%

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
Warning of a lack of hostel places for 2,000 criminals due to be released over the next month to ease overcrowding
Hundreds of prisoners are due to be released early from jail on Thursday amid warnings that many will have nowhere to live and the probation system will struggle to monitor them.
About 2,000 criminals including domestic abusers and violent offenders are to be freed over the next month, with another 3,000 in stages over the next year to ease overcrowding. The number was reduced from 6,000 after an intervention by the prime minister, Andy Burnham.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prisoners freed early in England and Wales risk living on the streets, say probation officers

articles.author: Jonathan Yerushalmy
articles.description:
Israeli prime minister cautions against early conclusions when asked if there were any signs of Iranian involvement
Benjamin Netanyahu has said it was too early to tell who was ultimately behind the apparent attempt to crash a ⁠Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight, even as Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations called the incident a “terror attack”, without apportioning blame.
Danny Danon told Fox News on Wednesday night that Israel had “no doubt that it was a terror attack from a radical individual. We still cannot link it to a terror state or terror organisation, but for sure we know there was an intention to bring that plane down.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Netanyahu says too early to tell who was behind plane incident as flydubai halts all flights to Israel

articles.author: Guardian staff
articles.description:
Estonian completed first of two attempts to navigate narrow ribbon, 160 metres long and 120 metres high, near the city’s famous Gyeongbokgung palace on Thursday
Estonian aerial athlete Jaan Roose has completed his first crossing of a 160-metre long highline suspended 120 metres above central Seoul on Thursday.
Roose, a three-time slackline world champion, will step out on to a narrow polyester ribbon between the Koreana hotel and the Dong-A Media Center, near the capital city’s famous Gyeongbokgung palace and Gwanghwamun square.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Daredevil Jaan Roose completes slackline walk high above central Seoul

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo and Quique Kierszenbaum in Jerusalem; graphics by Ana Lucía González Paz
articles.description:
Some on streets of Jerusalem pledge their support to prime minister while others hope for change
On the streets of Jerusalem, crowded with secular and ultra-Orthodox Jews, religious nationalists, settlers, Palestinians, and soldiers returning from deployments, uncertainty hangs over an election less than a month away that could mark a turning point for a country profoundly changed after the Hamas attacks of 7 October 2023 and nearly three years of war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
The political battle remains on a knife-edge.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israelis divided as vote that could oust Netanyahu only weeks away

articles.author: Jason Burke and Eithne Staunton
articles.description:
Satellite imagery shows further destruction of homes, businesses and places of worship since fragile ceasefire 
An update to Google Maps has revealed the extent of devastation during the three-year Gaza war and the severity of the continuing humanitarian crisis faced by the territory’s 2.3 million inhabitants.
The images were taken in June this year and show further destruction of homes, businesses, places of worship and infrastructure since a fragile ceasefire came into effect almost 12 months ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New Google Maps images reveal massive scale of devastation in Gaza

articles.author: Ajit Niranjan
articles.description:
Alpine regions in Europe experiencing extreme glacier collapse due to heat-trapping effects of fossil fuel pollution
Switzerland has lost almost one-fifth of its ice in just five years, research has found, in a dramatic reshaping of the Alpine country whose big white glaciers have been reduced to moonlike rock deserts, scientists say.
Swiss glaciers shrank by 5.5% in the first eight months of 2026, according to an annual monitoring report, after a summer of scorching heatwaves that followed a winter with little snow. The reduction in ice volume falls just shy of the record set in 2022 and brings the total loss of glacier ice since 2021 to 19.4%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Explosion of melt rates’: 20% of Swiss glaciers lost in five years

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv
articles.description:
Olga Rudenko says news site has duty to report on Russian military gains and Ukrainian corruption even if subjects are not so well read
Readers of Ukraine’s leading English news site “really want Russia to suffer” but that should not lead the title to downplay the military and political problems facing Kyiv, its editor has said.
Speaking to the Guardian before an event to London, Olga Rudenko said many of the Kyiv Independent’s most-read stories described Ukrainian deep strike attacks into Russia, potentially distorting its coverage.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kyiv Independent editor: ‘Our readers want Russia to suffer but we can’t be propagandists’

articles.author: Maya Yang and agency
articles.description:
Christa Pike, sentenced to death over 1995 murder, was heard snoring 40 minutes after lethal doses administered, witnesses said
Tennessee officials were unable to carry out the execution of Christa Pike despite her being administered two doses of a lethal injection drug, her lawyers said, adding that she had been taken to hospital in an ambulance.
Her attorneys told a local news station “this has turned into agony and a violation of Pike’s right to be executed free of cruel and unusual punishment.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tennessee woman on death row taken to hospital after surviving two lethal injections

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Housemate tells court she saw the bags oozing red liquid she assumed was furniture rust
Jesse Baird’s housemate didn’t know she was looking at bags with Baird and his partner’s dead bodies, when she took a photo of oozing surfboard covers the night of their alleged murders, a court has heard.
Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024. He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jesse Baird’s housemate did not know surfboard bags contained bodies when she took photo, court hears

articles.author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
articles.description:
Warning comes as central bank estimates fewer than one in 100 borrowers owe more on their home than its worth

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Reserve Bank says households are well placed to weather the twin storm of rising interest rates and plunging property prices, but warned that Australia would not be immune to a sudden collapse of the global AI investment boom.
The central bank’s latest financial stability review – a biannual assessment of the financial system – said the “threats to global financial stability continue to mount”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia at risk from major global financial shock, Reserve Bank warns

articles.author: Petra Stock
articles.description:
BoM expects 30 to 50mm of rain to fall in Melbourne over coming days, with showers and storms also likely for Canberra and Sydney on Saturday

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Widespread rain and thunderstorms are forecast to drench south-eastern Australia from Thursday, with the heaviest falls expected across Victoria.
A trough moving east across South Australia was expected to combine with a low pressure system moving through the Great Australian Bight on Thursday, according to the Bureau of Meteorology.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Parts of Victoria could see three months’ worth of rain as storms forecast for Australia’s south-east

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo and agency
articles.description:
Suspect Benny Caldera Jr held on bond as officials say they received ‘credible’ information about Austin threat
A 40-year-old man was arrested early Wednesday on suspicion of plotting to attack the Texas state capitol, authorities said.
The Texas department of public safety said in a statement that it received “credible information about an individual planning a violent attack” for Thursday in Austin.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man arrested over alleged plot to attack Texas state capitol

articles.author: Emma Joyce
articles.description:
Tapes made in the 90s, including candid conversations between Noel and Liam Gallagher, which were expected to sell for up to £1.6m
A collection of unheard Oasis recordings, including 63 live shows, hours of rehearsals and candid conversations between Noel and Liam Gallagher, has been pulled from auction after legal action taken by the band.
In September Littleton Auctions in Worcestershire, England, listed the collection made by the band’s former sound engineer, Huw Richards, with a guide price of between £1.2m and £1.6m.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Oasis take legal action to stop sale of unheard recordings valued at more than £1m

articles.author: Abené Clayton
articles.description:
Officials investigating missing persons case find bodies in remote area of Lancaster, north of Los Angeles
Law enforcement officials are looking for additional victims after two bodies were found on Tuesday in a remote area of Lancaster, California, a small city about 70 miles north of Los Angeles, the Los Angeles Times reports.
Authorities found the bodies in a shallow grave while they were investigating a missing persons case, according to KTLA. Outside of the sheriff’s department investigating the discovery of the remains as a homicide, little is known about the two people who were found in the shallow grave.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Police search for additional victims as two bodies discovered in California

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Democratic governor sharply critical of Donald Trump for not passing comprehensive federal AI regulations
Governor Gavin Newsom signed laws Wednesday aimed at protecting California workers from the threats of artificial intelligence , including potential job losses and workplace surveillance.
The laws ban employers from using the technology to predict a worker’s emotional state by using their biometric data, require employers to send written notices to workers if AI is responsible for mass layoffs and ban employers from relying on AI to decide to fire someone.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gavin Newsom signs laws to protect California workers from AI threat

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
Noem cites irreconcilable differences in filing that comes after husband Bryon Noem involved in tabloid scandal
Kristi Noem, who was fired by Donald Trump after a rumbustious stint as homeland security secretary, is divorcing her husband, Bryon Noem, after 34 years of marriage, citing “irreconcilable differences”.
The divorce claim “for settlement purposes only” was disclosed in court records filed in Hamlin county, South Dakota, the state of which Noem was previously governor.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kristi Noem, former Trump homeland security chief, files for divorce

articles.author: Patrick Barkham
articles.description:
Simple deterrents can slash the number of razorbills and guillemots being trapped underwater, two-year study shows
Bird-shaped kites and a floating scarecrow are being tested to try to stop endangered seabirds drowning in fishing nets.
Every year an estimated 95,000 diving birds, including razorbills and guillemots, are accidentally caught in nets off European coasts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Floating scarecrows: how Cornish fishers are stopping seabirds drowning in their nets

articles.author: Esther Addley
articles.description:
Community-funded archaeological excavations of ‘really important’ sixth-century monastery also rewrite story of Lismore
To the residents of the Scottish island of Lismore, population 190, history is never very far away. The tiny island near Oban in Argyll has no row of shops or even a pub – if islanders want to meet for a coffee, the only place to do so is in the lively Gaelic heritage centre that records the many centuries of community life on the island.
This quiet place, documentary evidence records, was home to a monastic settlement in the sixth century AD, when missionaries from Ireland were first moving into northern Britain to spread Christianity. But apart from a few fragments of an early carved cross, there was almost nothing to see from this period of history.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Hugely exciting’ finds on tiny Scottish island shed light on spread of Christianity

articles.author: William Christou in Beirut and Andrew Roth in Washington
articles.description:
Accused pilot being questioned in Saudi Arabia as Israeli officials investigate if incident was attempted terror attack

‘Whoever is hearing me, we need help’: how flight 1073 survived its 17,000ft plunge

One of the pilots of a plane flying from the United Arab Emirates to Israel stabbed his co-pilot and appeared to try to crash the aircraft, the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has said, as Israeli officials said they were investigating whether the incident was an attempted terror attack on Israelis.
Eyewitnesses reported chaos onboard the flydubai flight, as the attacker tried to barricade himself and the wounded co-pilot in the cockpit, and then attempted to disable the controls, forcing the plane to descend 17,000 feet in just two minutes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pilot who stabbed co-pilot on Israel-bound plane may have tried to crash it, says Netanyahu

articles.author: Andrew Roth and Joseph Gedeon in Washington
articles.description:
Support such as for white Afrikaners and anti-communism reveals how US is redefining what qualifies as human rights
With hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a huge $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner rights in South Africa, a campaign against Brazil’s supreme court and programs that would reward ideological allies in Europe who protect “western civilizational norms”.
On Wednesday, the state department obligated the funds to the grantees hours before the deadline despite congressional concerns and requests not to do so, according to a source familiar with the negotiations. The state department declined to comment on questions from the Guardian specifically on whether it had obligated the funds and had “blown” holds from Congress due to concerns about the money’s use.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump administration diverts human rights funds to push far-right agenda abroad

articles.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Settler violence in West Bank makes everyday life ‘untenable’ for Palestinians, says ICRC after assault on family trying to return home in Jalud
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has said Israeli settler violence in the West Bank has made everyday life for Palestinians “untenable”, as a mob attack on Palestinians trying to return home prompted one of Benjamin Netanyahu’s main rivals to warn of a campaign of settler terror.
More than 100 militant settlers overwhelmed Israeli security forces early on Tuesday to attack a Palestinian family as they attempted to reclaim their homes which had been seized by settlers in the West Bank village of Jalud. Three Israeli security officials were injured and houses were set on fire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli forces overwhelmed by violent settlers in ‘terrorist attack’ on Palestinian family

articles.author: Jess Cartner-Morley in Paris
articles.description:
Designer showcases wool alternatives and ocean-inspired clothes and says ‘kindness requires real work’
Stella McCartney has been talking about animal rights at fashion week for 30 years. She is usually a lone voice, but the issue is back in the headlines this season. Outcry over the physical restraining of a Peta protester at a catwalk show by Steven Kolb, the president of New York fashion week’s governing body, has put cruelty in wool production – previously considered niche compared to the hot button topic of fur – on the news agenda.
“There is no wool on the runway this season, and I’m proud of that,” McCartney said after her show. She has been working on wool alternatives, including Brewed Protein, a fermented alternative to cashmere and wool developed in collaboration with the Japanese biotech firm Spiber, which was first used in her collections a year ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stella McCartney makes waves with ‘sea life, not sea food’ theme in zero-wool Paris show

articles.author: Kiran Stacey and Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
Senior Downing Street officials reach out to thinktanks and pollsters as they look to test backing for reversing Brexit
Senior Downing Street officials have been reaching out to thinktanks and pollsters as they look to test public support for the UK rejoining the EU.
Aides to Andy Burnham have been talking to EU experts in a range of organisations about how the public would view a promise to rejoin, as momentum builds behind including such a pledge in the next Labour manifesto.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No 10 gathering evidence on public support for UK rejoining EU

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
French president, speaking alongside Spanish counterpart Pedro Sánchez, says EU bid would be good news for UK and Europeans
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, has reacted warmly to Andy Burnham’s suggestion that the UK could rejoin the EU.
“Welcome back,” the French leader said in English with a smile at a news conference in Madrid on Wednesday. Macron continued in French: “If the British want to come back and if the prime minister is moving in that direction, I think that is very good news, both for his country and for the Europeans.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Macron says ‘welcome back’ to Burnham suggestion UK could rejoin EU

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Women say nothing has changed since Delhi’s infamous Nirbhaya bus rape case 14 years ago
The posters, just like the women holding them, were taking no prisoners. “Girls don’t need curfews, rapists need consequences,” read one. “Lock your dicks rather than your women at home,” read another.
As hundreds of women walked from the gates of their university campus into the streets of Delhi – where sexual harassment, assault, catcalling and molestation are a constant, daily threat – they shouted together in a chorus of rage and defiance: “We want justice.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We want justice’: series of rapes trigger mass protests at Indian universities

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
President announces measures amid anger at authorities over recent murders of women
South Africa’s president has called on men to take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced measures to tackle the problem, amid anger at authorities over a recent wave of murders.
Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women. He said police would be reviewing unsolved murders, attempted murders and serious sexual offences against women and children, as well as producing a funded plan to reduce the forensic backlog for such cases, both within 60 days.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South African leader urges men to speak up on gender-based violence after series of killings

articles.author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
articles.description:
Institutions have for years turned to China for funding opportunities but national security concerns are mounting

MI5 issues spy alert to UK universities over Chinese front company stealing research

The security alert issued by MI5 regarding a Chinese state-owned conglomerate accused of conducting espionage in the UK reveals the extent to which British intelligence remains concerned about Beijing’s influence, and risks casting a shadow over UK-China cooperation at a time when the bilateral relationship is enjoying a revival.
The UK’s domestic security service on Wednesday warned researchers and academics to cease work with the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT), an organisation MI5 described as a “significant threat”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities

articles.author: Vikram Dodd, Sally Weale, Simon Goodley and Richard Adams
articles.description:
Security service says academics should stop working with and taking grants from firm backed by Chinese intelligence

MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities

MI5 has issued a rare public warning to UK universities that China’s intelligence service is using a front company to pay for research by UK academics and steal the secrets of hi-tech projects.
Britain’s domestic security service said researchers and academics should cease work with the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI), sometimes also known as the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT).
Additional reporting by Helena Horton
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MI5 warns UK universities over ‘theft of tech secrets by Chinese front company’

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Burundi joins several other African nations in accepting people deported under Trump’s hardline policy
Burundi has agreed to join a clutch of ⁠other African nations in receiving migrants from other countries deported from the US under ⁠Donald Trump’s hardline ⁠immigration ​policy.
However, Burundi will only accept those not accused of crime or terrorism links, said ⁠Nancy Ninette Mutoni, a spokesperson for the country’s president, Évariste Ndayishimiye. Tuesday’s announcement gave no details of numbers, timing or financial ⁠details.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burundi agrees to receive ‘third-country’ migrant deportees from US

articles.author: Justin McCurry in Tokyo
articles.description:
Kenjiro Tsuda wins case against TikTok account in landmark Japanese verdict to protect publicity rights
A court in Japan has ruled that the human voice has legal protection after a landmark case involving a well-known actor and a TikTok account that he claimed had cloned his “lustrous” baritone voice in its AI-generated videos.
Tokyo district court said on Wednesday that voices should enjoy the same protection as publicity rights, at the end of a closely watched legal action brought against TikTok by Kenjiro Tsuda – best known for voicing the character Kento Nanami in the anime Jujutsu Kaisen.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI tool that copied actor’s ‘lustrous’ voice violated his rights, Tokyo court rules

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
Blast during search operation near border fuels political tensions amid attempts to revive diplomatic channels
South Korea has demanded an apology from North Korea over a landmine blast that injured three soldiers, saying they were hurt by North Korean mines on the southern side of the border.
Kang Hyun-woo, the director of operations at South Korea’s joint chiefs of staff, demanded an apology and “responsible measures” from Pyongyang over the blast, which occurred on 21 September during a search operation south of the border.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South Korea calls for apology from North Korea after mine injures three soldiers

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
As outrage grows over cases​ of sexual violence, activists are demanding a shift from controlling women to confronting men’s behaviour. Plus, Tony Klor’s ‘hella dope’ city vlogs
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
As an Indian woman, I often feel myself oscillating between states of anxiety or anger. The anxiety is about doing the mental maths of how to stay safe – thinking about what I’m wearing, where I am going and how I’ll get there, and so on. The anger is at the sheer absurdity of this, and the stories of of sexual violence and harassment I read about every day. I am not the only one.
Last week, two particularly enraging incidents captured national attention. First, a video showing a group of men accused of harassing and molesting two teenagers at night in Bihar’s Jamui went viral. Then, a 17-year-old, out with a friend in Delhi, was allegedly gang-raped in a park by men posing as police. After, women in Bihar told Outlook how the incident in Jamui triggers greater controls and pressure on them. In Delhi, authorities curbed access to public parks and a premier women’s college, Lady Shri Ram College (LSR), briefly moved classes online.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From Jamui to Delhi, the burden of safety from sexual assault cannot fall on women

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Marie-Celestin Karondwa was attacked on Sunday after promoting measures to prevent spread of disease, his party says

A senior member of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ruling party was beaten to death on Sunday after appearing on a radio programme to raise awareness about the Ebola outbreak, a party representative has said.
Marie-Celestin Karondwa, the acting president of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party’s federal executive committee in Butembo, a new hotspot for the outbreak, was attacked after taking part in a ​radio show during which he ‌promoted prevention measures for the disease, ‌the UDPS federation in the city said in a statement, Reuters reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: DRC politician beaten to death after radio appearance about Ebola outbreak

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Slinger Francisco, who performed as the Mighty Sparrow, died on Sunday surrounded by family in New York
Slinger Francisco, known on stage as the Mighty Sparrow and dubbed the “calypso king of the world”, has died aged 91.
Francisco, who got his breakthrough in calypso music with his 1956 hit song Jean and Dinah, died peacefully surrounded by his family in New York on Sunday, his family said in a statement.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mighty Sparrow, the Trinidad and Tobago singer known as the ‘calypso king of the world’, dies aged 91

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Hurricane Nolo is moving away from Hawaiian islands but threat of heavy rain, flash floods and strong winds persists
Hurricane Nolo was moving away from the Hawaiian islands on Sunday, but the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding and strong winds persisted in areas of the island chain still recovering from previous storms.
Nolo was about 365 miles (585km) south-south-west of Honolulu and moving away from the Big Island at about 12mph (19km/h). But the Hawaii county civil defense agency said a high wind warning, wind advisory and high surf advisory remained in effect for parts of the island through Sunday evening as Nolo’s maximum sustained winds rose to 115mph.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hurricane Nolo still threatens Hawaii as Mexico’s Baja braces for Hurricane Polo

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg and agencies
articles.description:
Seventeen people killed near Johannesburg in suspected ‘illegal goldmining turf war’, as 10 killed in separate incident at barbecue venue near Cape Town
Two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, as the country grapples with one of the world’s highest murder rates amid investigations into corruption and criminality within the police.
The South African police service said on Sunday that 17 people were killed on Saturday night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 assault rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, about 50 miles south-west of central Johannesburg. At least 15 other people sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least 27 dead after two mass shootings in South Africa, police say

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
Loved ones describe Jordan Yap, 30, as an experienced hiker who set out for a 10-day solo trek Peru before falling silent

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Loved ones of a missing Australian trekker who was last seen nearly two weeks ago on a remote South American hiking trail are urging local authorities to help with the search.
A wide-scale sweep by a private rescue crew has so far failed to find any trace of 30-year-old Jordan Yap, who last made contact with friends and family on 14 September ahead of a planned 10-day solo trek along Peru’s Huayhuash mountain range, 400km north-east of Lima.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Melbourne man’s mysterious disappearance on popular Peru hiking trail prompts widespread search

articles.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
articles.description:
Attorney says fishers ‘losing their livelihoods’, but Marco Rubio maintains US still willing to ‘blow up ships if need be’
While the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, was being decorated in Quito by Ecuador’s president for “helping to promote peace in the region”, 10 Ecuadorian fishers whose boat had been blown up by US forces were adrift in the eastern Pacific.
On 8 September, a day before Rubio arrived, a US patrol vessel intercepted the fishing boat Don Rufo in international waters near Ecuador.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US strikes on Ecuadorian fishing boats raise humanitarian concerns but Trump admin not wavering

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
President’s ‘hard, drastic and necessary measure’, likely to attract widespread public support, polls suggest
The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has signed an order banning fixed-odds sports betting just over a week before the first round of the presidential election, in a move he said was designed to tackle the pervasive problem of families falling into debt.
The decision ends the operation, offering, intermediation and advertising of betting.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lula bans fixed-odds sports betting a week before Brazilian elections

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad and Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Tens of thousands of police deployed and roads barricaded as PTI party demands release of jailed former PM
Leaders from Imran Khan’s party have vowed to go ahead with a nationwide demonstration in Pakistan to demand the former prime minister’s release, even as the government deployed tens of thousands of police to Islamabad, barricaded highways and issued arrest warrants to try to stop the march.
The state has taken extreme measures to prevent Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party from proceeding with the march. It was announced after mounting concerns of the treatment of Khan, who has been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan locks down Islamabad as Imran Khan’s party vows to march on capital

articles.author: Rachel Hall and Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
Role for Anant Ambani, son of India’s richest person, who also runs a controversial mega-zoo, met with incredulity
Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability.
The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Backlash as Indian oil heir made professor of sustainability by Newcastle University

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Islamic State-inspired bombings of churches and hotels in 2019 was one of the country’s worst ever attacks
A court in Sri Lanka has convicted 15 men on terrorist charges for their involvement in the deadly 2019 Easter bombings and sentenced them each to at least 220 years in prison.
The terror attacks, which targeted luxury hotels and churches as they held Easter services, left 267 people dead and wounded almost 600. The bombings, which were inspired by Islamic State (IS), were among the deadliest terror attacks in Sri Lanka’s history and sent shockwaves through the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings: 15 sentenced to hundreds of years in prison each over deadly terror attacks

articles.author: Lauren Gambino
articles.description:
The candidates running to replace Gavin Newsom sparred over taxes, immigration and regulating AI
Xavier Becerra and Steve Hilton, the candidates running to be California’s next governor, clashed Wednesday over taxes, immigration and regulating artificial intelligence in a testy debate held days before voters begin receiving their ballots in the heavily Democratic state.
Hilton, the former Fox News host endorsed by Donald Trump, used the hourlong matchup, hosted by CNN, to argue that Becerra, a former congressman who served as health and human services secretary during the Biden administration, was not actively campaigning and instead taking voters for granted.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Steve Hilton, Xavier Becerra clash in testy California governor’s race debate

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Hegseth confirms plan to cut 20% of US top military brass and rails at ‘beardos, weirdos and wimps’

Sign up for the Breaking News US email

Rachel Leingang and Riley Messer
Some of the biggest food and agriculture corporations in the US are funding a campaign that pays social media influencers to combat elements of Robert F Kennedy Jr’s Make America Healthy Again platform, according to an investigation by the Guardian and Documented, an investigative watchdog and journalism project.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hegseth says he will cut number of US generals by 20% in anti-diversity speech – as it happened

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo and agency
articles.description:
Suspect Benny Caldera Jr held on bond as officials say they received ‘credible’ information about Austin threat
A 40-year-old man was arrested early Wednesday on suspicion of plotting to attack the Texas state capitol, authorities said.
The Texas department of public safety said in a statement that it received “credible information about an individual planning a violent attack” for Thursday in Austin.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man arrested over alleged plot to attack Texas state capitol

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
Noem cites irreconcilable differences in filing that comes after husband Bryon Noem involved in tabloid scandal
Kristi Noem, who was fired by Donald Trump after a rumbustious stint as homeland security secretary, is divorcing her husband, Bryon Noem, after 34 years of marriage, citing “irreconcilable differences”.
The divorce claim “for settlement purposes only” was disclosed in court records filed in Hamlin county, South Dakota, the state of which Noem was previously governor.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kristi Noem, former Trump homeland security chief, files for divorce

articles.author: Shrai Popat in Washington and Ariana Baio in New York City
articles.description:
Amid latest extraordinary attack on diversity, US defense secretary also suggests military is retaining service personnel at ‘record’ rates

Send us your questions about how the Iran war will affect US voters in the midterms

The US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, has confirmed plans to cut 20% of generals and admirals and declared “no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps” would be tolerated inside the country’s military.
Delivering his latest extraordinary attack on diversity, and dismissing reports of low morale within the US armed forces as “false claims”, Hegseth also suggested they were retaining service personnel at “record” rates.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hegseth confirms plan to cut 20% of US top military brass and rails at ‘beardos, weirdos and wimps’

articles.author: Guardian staff
articles.description:
Late-night hosts weighed in on Trump’s relationship with tech leaders and the White House’s new AI-powered site
On Tuesday night, late-night hosts discussed a Maha summit in Washington DC, the White House’s new AI-powered website and Donald Trump once again falling asleep on live TV.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Seth Meyers on Trump canceling $1bn in federal funds: ‘Is he adding a waterslide to the reflecting pool?’

articles.author: Andrew Gumbel in Los Angeles
articles.description:
Steve Hilton’s long-shot campaign for governor is courting Golden state voters with unapologetically populist message
Steve Hilton stands almost no chance of becoming California’s next governor, but that isn’t stopping him from campaigning as though he was just one step away from pulling off the impossible.
The former Downing Street political adviser and Fox News host refuses to be daunted by the rancid political environment for Republican candidates this year, or by opinion polls that tell him he is lagging 20 percentage points or more behind his Democratic rival, Xavier Becerra.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Of course I’m the underdog’: the British former spin doctor trying to turn California red

articles.author: Tom Phillips, Bryony Moore, Karif Wat and Boglarka Kosztolanyi
articles.description:
Brazil will head to the polls on 4 October for the first vote in its presidential race. The incumbent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, is neck-and-neck with Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of the former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is in prison for plotting a military coup. There are fears and accusations that the US is interfering in the election, and these follow similar allegations in a string of elections across Latin America won by Donald Trump-backed candidates in what is being called 'the orange wave'.
The Guardian's Latin America correspondent, Tom Phillips, explains the tactics Trump and his administration have been using in recent months and what impact another Bolsonaro government could have on the region, and the world
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Trump is meddling in Brazil's election – explainer

articles.author: Stephen Starr in Dearborn, Michigan
articles.description:
Arab communities on both sides of the border grapple with ongoing tensions as US-Canada relations continue to sour
In Dearborn, Michigan, home to the largest community of Arab Americans in the US, one industry has risen above all others in recent years: Yemeni cafes.
At the forefront is Qahwah House, a powerhouse in the burgeoning Yemeni cafe world with 32 branches open across the country. Three of those are here in Dearborn, with more on the way, and they attract people from near and far.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘So much uncertainty’: Michigan’s Arab American businesses navigate Trump’s Canada trade war

articles.author: Alexandra Villarreal
articles.description:
After switching tactics, federal agents are detaining and deporting record numbers of people from the US

Gone in 90 seconds: an ‘invisibilized’ ICE is arresting more people than ever

Three deaths, three states, 24 hours: one day in ICE’s quiet but ‘gruesome’ surge

When federal agents fatally shot the US citizen protesters Alex Pretti and Renee Good in Minneapolis in January during the nation’s largest immigration-enforcement operation ever, it marked a turning point for the second Trump administration’s mass deportation campaign.
Donald Trump in his second term had sparked outrage and huge protests with federal immigration officers descending en masse on one Democratic-run city after another in what some leaders called militarized “invasions”. Los Angeles, Chicago, Charlotte, New Orleans, then Minneapolis saw lines of masked and armored officers swaggering into town to conduct street arrests, ambushes of day workers waiting in Home Depot car parks for hire, and neighborhood sweeps. Adults and kids were whisked off to detention and protests met with aggressive deployment of chemical spray, teargas, fists and batons. The killings in Minneapolis were the culmination of what appeared to many to be a federal shock force increasingly out of control while being defended by federal leaders – and public opinion broadly turned against this violence.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From mass raids to quiet crackdown: a timeline of Trump’s strategic ICE pivot

articles.author: Sidney Blumenthal
articles.description:
The Texas Senate candidate rose to power as a culture warrior. His record is a marriage of hypocrisy and cynicism
Ken Paxton’s political career, more than that of any other Republican candidate campaigning in this cycle, charts the arc of the religious right. The most influential of its activists and donors engineered his rise as a culture warrior at each of its phases from his creation through every disgrace. His race for the Senate, the culmination of his ambition, has become not only his last stand, but also the Alamo for Christian nationalists in Texas.
Paxton’s rap sheet explains his Christian identity politics as a shield to distract from the liability of his own record of financial and sexual scandals scrolling back decades. The 20 articles of impeachment against Paxton, adopted by the Republican-controlled Texas house of representatives in May 2023, were double the Ten Commandments that Paxton insists should be displayed in every Texas classroom.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ken Paxton’s Christian identity politics obscure a history of scandal | Sidney Blumenthal

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
With the midterms looming, and after the Epstein files and the war on Iran, Trump superfans are losing faith in their lame duck president
It took a dead child sex offender and a disastrous war to do it, but it looks as though the Maga faithful are slowly beginning to lose confidence in their dear leader. As Donald Trump’s approval ratings drop to record lows, some of his most fervent supporters are turning on him.
See, as exhibit one, Trisha Hope, who was once a proud member of the Front Row Joes, a group of Trump superfans who follow the president to rallies around the country. They have custom-made T-shirts! They have branded baseball caps! They even have the attention of Trump himself, who frequently shouts out the group. He did once accidentally call them the “front row Jacks and Joes”, but who can expect a man of his calibre to pay attention to the plebs, eh?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Donald Trump's Maga cult is finally crumbling | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: David Walbert
articles.description:
Republicans could lean on congressional procedure to defy the will of voters. But if they try that, the Senate has a clear way to fight back
Having lost his mail-in ballot case, Donald Trump will probably resort to ever more extreme ways to try to hold a Republican Congress in November’s elections.
His last-ditch effort to count Joe Biden out in 2020 was for Republicans to “investigate” states Biden narrowly won; proclaim fabricated allegations of “stolen elections” to be true; and then reassign those states’ electoral votes to Trump. I have previously described how that same playbook could be used to try to steal the midterms if a Democratic margin of victory in the House is relatively narrow.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Senate Democrats can stop Trump from stealing the midterms | David Walbert

articles.author: Moira Donegan
articles.description:
The US has already grown used to the horror caused by abortion bans. And Republicans have sought to quash the stories
Abortion has faded from the headlines since the Dobbs decision of 2022, and Republicans like it that way. In the immediate aftermath of the supreme court’s overturning of Roe v Wade, as millions of women lost access to the dignity and self-determination that abortion provided them, clinics shut their doors, and the extent of Dobbs’s horrendously adverse public health implications started to become clear, abortion was always, it seemed, in the headlines. There were plenty of stories. There was the first known woman to die as the result of an abortion ban; and then the second; and then the third. There were the various lawsuits and ballot initiatives that for a while turned a…
articles.title: Why has abortion faded from America’s national conversation? | Moira Donegan

articles.author: Marina Hyde, Nosheen Iqbal, Laurence Topham, Ruth Abrahams, Ben Kape and Sami Kent
articles.description:
The Guardian’s award-winning columnist talks to Nosheen Iqbal about Donald Trump's ballroom, going for a drink with Nigel Farage, Taylor Swift’s wedding, and why she's feeling relaxed about the AI apocalypse
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Marina Hyde on Trump's home improvements, tech bros and Taylor Swift – video

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland , with Shrai Popat , produced by Danielle Stephens and Nada Smiljanic
articles.description:
The US press corps stood up to Donald Trump this week after he banned three organisations he doesn’t like from the White House. But when it came to the leader of one of the US’s oldest adversaries – China – well, Trump literally rolled out a very long red carpet. Jonathan Freedland speaks to the Guardian’s Shrai Popat about why Trump seems weaker these days, but why it could be dangerous to underestimate him
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump picked a fight with the media... and lost | Politics Weekly America

articles.description:
CNN senior reporter Betsy Klein gained access to the White House on 24 September, hours after a federal judge ruled against Donald Trump's media ban. The ban had barred reporters from CNN, MS Now and Politico from accessing the White House
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CNN reporter arrives at White House after judge rules against Trump's media ban – video

articles.author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
articles.description:
Warning of a lack of hostel places for 2,000 criminals due to be released over the next month to ease overcrowding
Hundreds of prisoners are due to be released early from jail on Thursday amid warnings that many will have nowhere to live and the probation system will struggle to monitor them.
About 2,000 criminals including domestic abusers and violent offenders are to be freed over the next month, with another 3,000 in stages over the next year to ease overcrowding. The number was reduced from 6,000 after an intervention by the prime minister, Andy Burnham.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Prisoners freed early in England and Wales risk living on the streets, say probation officers

articles.author: Heather Stewart, Richard Partington and Jillian Ambrose
articles.description:
Millions of people in Great Britain face increase from Thursday to an average of £1,723 a year for a typical home
John Healey is under growing pressure to offer fresh energy support for households in next month’s budget as millions face a 4% rise in charges from Thursday to an average of £1,723 a year for a typical home.
In his speech at Labour’s conference in Liverpool this week, the chancellor warned that the government had limited resources to cushion the worldwide economic shocks hitting Britain, while arguing his budget would have fiscal discipline at its core.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healey urged to offer energy support in budget as bills rise 4%

articles.author: Shane Hickey
articles.description:
The Naylors’ four-bedroom home in Milton Keynes acts like a mini-power station after retrofitting solar panels, a battery and a heat pump
Clare Naylor paid close attention to how much energy she and her family were using last winter, filling hot-water bottles and bringing out extra blankets to ensure they didn’t go over budget. This year, she won’t have to worry as she is guaranteed not to receive a bill.
While millions of British households face the highest energy charges in three years from today after a 4% rise in the price cap, and predictions of a 16% increase in January, upgrades to Naylor’s home mean she will not have to pay anything.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The zero-bills home: how one family is beating the energy price hikes

articles.author: Emma Joyce
articles.description:
Tapes made in the 90s, including candid conversations between Noel and Liam Gallagher, which were expected to sell for up to £1.6m
A collection of unheard Oasis recordings, including 63 live shows, hours of rehearsals and candid conversations between Noel and Liam Gallagher, has been pulled from auction after legal action taken by the band.
In September Littleton Auctions in Worcestershire, England, listed the collection made by the band’s former sound engineer, Huw Richards, with a guide price of between £1.2m and £1.6m.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Oasis take legal action to stop sale of unheard recordings valued at more than £1m

articles.author: Patrick Barkham
articles.description:
Simple deterrents can slash the number of razorbills and guillemots being trapped underwater, two-year study shows
Bird-shaped kites and a floating scarecrow are being tested to try to stop endangered seabirds drowning in fishing nets.
Every year an estimated 95,000 diving birds, including razorbills and guillemots, are accidentally caught in nets off European coasts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Floating scarecrows: how Cornish fishers are stopping seabirds drowning in their nets

articles.author: Esther Addley
articles.description:
Community-funded archaeological excavations of ‘really important’ sixth-century monastery also rewrite story of Lismore
To the residents of the Scottish island of Lismore, population 190, history is never very far away. The tiny island near Oban in Argyll has no row of shops or even a pub – if islanders want to meet for a coffee, the only place to do so is in the lively Gaelic heritage centre that records the many centuries of community life on the island.
This quiet place, documentary evidence records, was home to a monastic settlement in the sixth century AD, when missionaries from Ireland were first moving into northern Britain to spread Christianity. But apart from a few fragments of an early carved cross, there was almost nothing to see from this period of history.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Hugely exciting’ finds on tiny Scottish island shed light on spread of Christianity

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Unionists spurn NI secretary’s attempt to resolve impasse after nationalists block controversial Garvaghy Road march
Talks to end the Drumcree parade dispute are on a knife-edge after Jamie Bryson, the legal adviser of the Orange Order, said it would “not surrender” to a deal proposed by the Northern Ireland secretary, Chris Bryant.
With echoes of the former Democratic Unionist leader Ian Paisley’s “no surrender” mantra of the 1980s, Bryson told supporters in Portadown that Bryant could keep his deal.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Drumcree standoff continues after Orange Order says it will ‘not surrender’ to proposed deal

articles.author: Kiran Stacey and Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
Senior Downing Street officials reach out to thinktanks and pollsters as they look to test backing for reversing Brexit
Senior Downing Street officials have been reaching out to thinktanks and pollsters as they look to test public support for the UK rejoining the EU.
Aides to Andy Burnham have been talking to EU experts in a range of organisations about how the public would view a promise to rejoin, as momentum builds behind including such a pledge in the next Labour manifesto.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: No 10 gathering evidence on public support for UK rejoining EU

articles.author: Ben Quinn and Peter Walker
articles.description:
Met calls move ‘milestone’ moment that paves way for ‘very best possible evidence for charging decisions’
Police investigating the Grenfell Tower fire have asked prosecutors to consider charges including manslaughter and fraud against a range of companies and individuals.
The Metropolitan police announced they had given prosecutors evidence relating to 20 companies and organisations and 54 individuals ahead of charging decisions, in what the force described as a “milestone moment”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Grenfell police hand files on 20 organisations and 54 people to CPS

articles.author: Eve Livingston
articles.description:
The Traitors and big film shoots help boost economy but some highlight lack of opportunities for local talent
Scotland’s striking Ardross Castle, the oldest star of The Celebrity Traitors, which kicks off on Thursday night, is just one of the stops on the Scottish tourist board’s “screen tourism” trail. From Outlander and The Odyssey filming in the Highlands and islands, to Glasgow city centre standing in for New York and Gotham City in the latest instalments of Indiana Jones and Batman respectively, film and TV is increasingly big business in Scotland.
The country’s screen sector, growing year on year, is projected to be worth £1bn to the economy by 2030. But while some have celebrated the upsides of a booming production sector, others highlight a lack of opportunities for Scottish talent and the challenges of excessive tourism in areas featured on screen.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scottish screen sector boom brings questions over jobs and overtourism

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
French president, speaking alongside Spanish counterpart Pedro Sánchez, says EU bid would be good news for UK and Europeans
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, has reacted warmly to Andy Burnham’s suggestion that the UK could rejoin the EU.
“Welcome back,” the French leader said in English with a smile at a news conference in Madrid on Wednesday. Macron continued in French: “If the British want to come back and if the prime minister is moving in that direction, I think that is very good news, both for his country and for the Europeans.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Macron says ‘welcome back’ to Burnham suggestion UK could rejoin EU

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
articles.description:
Developing North Sea fields does not contradict net zero goals, according to Simone Rossi
New oil and gas projects are a “no-brainer” that pose “no contradiction” to the net zero agenda, according to the head of EDF Energy.
Simone Rossi has joined a string of renewables leaders in making the case for more North Sea production as the government prepares to decide on two projects there.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New UK gas and oil projects are a ‘no-brainer’, says EDF boss

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
PM also defends decision to release suspects on bail and expresses ‘complete confidence’ in security services
There are “strong indications” that Iran played a role in events in which five men were arrested near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire as part of a terror investigation, Andy Burnham has said.
Speaking to the media at the end of the Labour party conference in Liverpool, Burnham said he could not give any more details amid a police investigation, but that Iran was believed to be involved.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Strong indications’ that Iran played role in RAF Fairford incident, says Burnham

articles.author: Zoe Wood
articles.description:
The price cap is to soar for about 20 million households in Great Britain from January, but there are ways to save

Energy bills in Great Britain forecast to jump by £276 a year from January

Household energy prices are set to soar in January, with a typical bill forecast to jump by £276 to the equivalent of nearly £2,000 year.
It is a worrying outlook but there are practical steps you can take to mitigate the predicted price shock.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Energy bills: what to do as prices head for £2,000 a year, from switching deals to insulating

articles.author: Jessica Elgot
articles.description:
Prime minister’s pure political argument marks new era for party as he sets out his plans and priorities
The hottest ticket at Labour conference – after Andy Burnham’s speech – was an afterparty in Liverpool’s Baltic Triangle, headlined with a set by the noughties girlband Sugababes. As Labour activists and ministers belted out the lyrics under pink spotlights, it was hard not to draw some parallels with the party’s recent history.
There have been painful lineup changes and a lot of internal division, but this week onstage in Liverpool the originals are back together and they only played the hits. The fans can’t get enough.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘He persuaded us’: Labour ministers moved by Andy Burnham’s emotional conference speech

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
articles.description:
Andrew Bailey’s comments come as fears grow that rogue models could take financial system hostage

Business live – latest updates

The governor of the Bank of England has called for the “right to intervene” in the AI industry amid growing fears that rogue models could take the financial system hostage.
Andrew Bailey said the risks posed by frontier AI models – a number of which have gone rogue in recent months – were “real and increasingly significant”. Meanwhile, it was becoming harder for the public to have proper oversight of powerful AI models that were “functioning within a self-reinforcing loop”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: We need ‘right to intervene’ in AI amid growing threat, says Bank of England boss

articles.author: Robert Booth UK technology editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Campaign comes amid backlash against tech company’s involvement with Israeli military and Trump’s ICE crackdown

UK politics live – latest updates

Tens of thousands of people have formally demanded NHS England blocks the Palantir-powered national medical data platform from handling their personal information.
More than 44,000 people have filed legal objections to their health data being shared with, stored in or used by the nationwide Federated Data Platform (FDP) operated using the US company’s AI technology.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: More than 44,000 file legal objections to Palantir NHS platform handling their data

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Boost for John Healey before budget as GDP figure shows UK economy grew faster than first estimated in second quarter
UK household income grew at a stronger pace than previously estimated during the first six months of the year, according to revisions of official data.
The rise in income per head to 1.1% between January and June followed an increase in the level of economic growth that illustrated the resilience of the UK economy since the outbreak of hostilities in the Middle East more than seven months ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK income growth revised upwards as markets hail ‘resilient’ economy

articles.author: Matthew Taylor
articles.description:
Environment Agency warns residents of 6m at-risk properties to prepare for wet and windy three months ahead
More than two million people in England are unaware their properties are at risk of flooding, as the UK braces for a wet and stormy start to the winter, according to the Environment Agency.
Experts say the next three months are more likely than usual to be wet and windy – due to a combination of large-scale weather patterns and the “subtle” impact of a supercharged El Niño – increasing the risk of flooding.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two million people in England unaware their properties are at risk of flooding

articles.author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
articles.description:
Institutions have for years turned to China for funding opportunities but national security concerns are mounting

MI5 issues spy alert to UK universities over Chinese front company stealing research

The security alert issued by MI5 regarding a Chinese state-owned conglomerate accused of conducting espionage in the UK reveals the extent to which British intelligence remains concerned about Beijing’s influence, and risks casting a shadow over UK-China cooperation at a time when the bilateral relationship is enjoying a revival.
The UK’s domestic security service on Wednesday warned researchers and academics to cease work with the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT), an organisation MI5 described as a “significant threat”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: MI5 China alert will send chill through UK’s cash-strapped universities

articles.author: Antonio Voce and Ashley Kirk
articles.description:
These visualisations from exclusive polling modelling show how the UK parliament could change under different voting systems
New analysis produced exclusively for the Guardian reveals how different voting systems would return significantly different seat totals in the UK parliament, based on recent polling.
While the current first past the post (FPTP) system could leave Labour short of a majority with 250 seats, the modelling shows how proportional systems would be likely to reduce the number of seats given to the leading party – and give the UK a more finely balanced parliament that better represents the votes people cast.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How could Great Britain look under proportional representation? See the results for your area

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed

‘Oozing everyman charm’: what the papers said about Burnham’s speech

Andy Burnham has suggested that it would not be legitimate for a party to form a majority government with less than 30% of the vote.
In his Today interview, asked why he wanted electoral reform and a move towards proportional representation, Burnham replied:
I found it better being elected under a different system as mayor of Greater Manchester, where people had one or two, they could put that on the ballot paper.
Because you had a reason to stop on every doorstep and chat to people who might not always support your party and try and get their second preference.
No, it could happen with any political party. It’s whether that would be a legitimate government.
I think you’ve got it completely wrong really, if you don’t mind me saying, to put it like that, because I have put out … a vision for a national care service.
There are pensioners out there who watch your programme who are paying for care costs from their basic state pension. Now, is that right or fair?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Voters back Burnham’s plan to cut back triple lock to fund social care reform by 48% to 28%, poll suggests – as it happened

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
PM’s oratory at least as good as Blair’s, says Andrew Marr, while Mail asks who pays for Honest Andy’s ‘New Jerusalem’
When assessing British political speeches, even many critics of the New Labour years measure success against Tony Blair, a leader whose podium appearances are regarded as the peak of oratory.
On that measure, Andrew Marr, the former BBC political editor and now the New Statesman’s chief political commentator, reached for the ultimate accolade. “Rather to my surprise, I have to report Andy Burnham is at least as good a platform speaker” as Blair, he said. “Perhaps better.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Oozing everyman charm’: what the papers say about Andy Burnham’s speech

articles.author: Matthew Taylor
articles.description:
Study says UK-based banks provided $8.3bn in coal financing in four years, with Barclays and HSBC leading rise
UK banks are Europe’s biggest financial backers of the global coal industry, providing billions of pounds in funding for the climate-wrecking fossil fuel in the past four years, according to a report.
The study found UK-based banks had provided $8.3bn (£6.2bn) in coal financing since Cop26 in Glasgow in 2021, when global leaders pledged to “phase down” coal use. This compared with $4.9bn from German banks and $3.4bn from French banks over the same period.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK banks are Europe’s biggest coal financiers, report finds

articles.author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
articles.description:
PM has revealed more details about a proposed shake-up of adult social care – including a broad timetable
Andy Burnham’s Labour conference speech gave a little more detail on how he intends to take forward what he said at the start of his premiership would be his signature social policy ambition: an overhaul of adult social care.
This article was updated after official clarifications on future care policy plans were issued
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How will Burnham’s national care service work – and how will it be funded?

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Bakery chain, whose sales are up 7.7%, says move is necessary to provide growth in ‘most cost-efficient manner’

Business live – latest updates

Greggs has announced plans to close four of its factories, in a move that could result in 740 job losses over the next two and a half years.
The bakery chain said it was consulting on the closures, which would initially cost £60m when including disruption costs and redundancy payments but then could create £20m of savings each year by 2028.

articles.title: Greggs announces plans to shut four UK factories that could cost 740 jobs

articles.author: Anna Bawden Health and social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Many products aimed at women over 45 lack meaningful quantities of key nutrients, consumer watchdog Which? found
Menopause supplements costing more than £400 a year are no better than a £22-a-year multivitamin, according to analysis by the consumer watchdog Which?.
Which? found that many popular supplements that are aimed at women over 45 going through menopause or perimenopause lack meaningful quantities of key nutrients, yet cost 20 times more than standard multivitamins.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Menopause supplements costing more than £400 a year ‘no better than cheap multivitamin’

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll, senior correspondent
articles.description:
The PM said Brexit has ‘done more harm than good’ and wants an assessment before the next UK-EU summit
Andy Burnham has said Brexit has “done more harm than good” and pledged to launch a major review of the UK’s relationship with the EU, opening the door to a potential referendum over rejoining the union.
He said he would “lay out options” around the time of the next EU-UK summit, due to be held at the end of November or soon after.

articles.author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
articles.description:
National Trust says latest figures encouraging – with numbers of birds on the rise – but work still to be done
England’s most important tern colonies are showing signs of recovery after being hit by years of bird flu, flooding and increasingly unpredictable weather, new figures from the National Trust reveal.
The trust reported record numbers of little terns at Long Nanny in Northumberland, one of the UK’s most important breeding sites for what is the country’s second-rarest breeding seabird.

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Exeter museum to host DJ’s ‘collaboration’ with woodland fungi and artist’s map of her own body’s mycobiome
For one of the installations, a musician spent hours in woodland “collaborating” with fungi to create a soundscape inspired by the electricity they emit.
Another is a kinetic sculpture of an extinct fungus that honours Beatrix Potter not for her tales of mischievous rabbits but for her lesser-known skills as a mycologist – a fungi expert.

articles.description:
District judge orders record fine for region and says incidents of pollution cannot be tolerated
A water company has been ordered to pay a record fine of almost £8m for hundreds of sewage spills at popular bathing spots and sensitive habitats in Cornwall and Devon.
On one occasion, untreated sewage gushed through a harbour wall on a bank holiday weekend but South West Water (SWW) engineers took 10 hours to attend.
 Continue reading...

Andy Burnham appeared on the verge of tears as he paid tribute to his father, Roy, on the second day of the party conference. The prime minister said he was 'utterly determined' to ensure the UK, which had given his dad 'a good life', stayed united

UK politics: latest updates

articles.author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
articles.description:
Rome, From Mount Aventine will also visit Hong Kong and New York before it is expected to sell for record price
A JMW Turner painting of Rome that has been described as his “great love letter” to the city and has fleetingly returned there after almost 200 years is expected to set a new record when it goes up for sale in December.
One of the few works by Turner that remains in private ownership, Rome, From Mount Aventine will be on display at Palazzo Rondinini in central Rome from Tuesday to Thursday.

articles.title: JMW Turner’s ‘great love letter’ to Rome makes brief return to city before UK auction

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Government decision comes in response to Margaret Hodge review that proposed charging international tourists
Overseas visitors will continue to enjoy free entry to England’s national museums after ministers decided against charging them after months of discussions between the government, museums, the tourism sector and local leaders.
Ministers said in March that “charging international visitors at national museums could provide significant benefits” as they promised to explore options including examining whether making overseas tourists pay could boost the institutions’ finances.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: England’s national museums to remain free to overseas visitors

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
NHS trusts also report disruption to supplies last winter of co-codamol and blood pressure medication ramipril
Hospitals are being hit by shortages of key drugs used to provide pain relief, prevent blood clots and tackle high blood pressure.
Dozens of NHS trusts in England have encountered scarcities of aspirin, the painkiller co-codamol – a combination of paracetamol and codeine – and ramipril, a blood pressure tablet.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hospitals in England hit by shortages of common drugs such as paracetamol

She also challenged Reform UK and the Tories on their climate inaction, saying they would eventually ‘bow’ because they were on the ‘wrong side of history’

articles.title: ‘They will bow’: energy secretary challenges Reform and Tories – podcast

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
People living next to a chemicals plant near Blackpool were tested for ‘forever chemicals’. Last week they received the alarming results
Last February, I got a call from a woman called Sam Hammond. We had been speaking on and off for a while over her growing concern that her garden could be affected by pollution from a nearby chemical plant.
That morning, Sam had been hand-delivered a letter from her council informing her that her pet ducks’ eggs, reared in her garden, were contaminated with Pfas chemicals.

articles.author: Kalyeena Makortoff in Jersey
articles.description:
While global billionaires and multinational companies have been lured to its shores, many islanders feel left behind and priced out, with food bank use increasing
On a late Friday afternoon on the Channel Island of Jersey, tourists and locals are flocking to St Helier’s waterfront where the town’s sprawling beach has emerged at low tide.
In one direction, they face the calm waters of St Aubin’s Bay, ringed by a seaside promenade and punctuated with a tidal island hosting the 16th century Elizabeth Castle.

From ‘there were three of us in this marriage’ to ‘recollections may vary’, a lot can be conveyed with a carefully worded phrase

Researching the history of the area as part of Cân y Cymoedd (When Valleys Sing), a project in nearby Port Talbot, she came across the story of Isabel Thomas, a 14-year-old girl in the 1940s who left school and lied about her age to work in a tin plate works to support her family.

articles.title: ‘Songwriting instead of doomscrolling’: project inspires Welsh valleys towns to tune into their heritage

articles.author: Kate Lamb

Some experts fear AI could be weaponised in south-east Asia, home to nations with predominately young and hyper-connected populations
Years ago it would have been an elaborate operation involving an army of cyber troops creating fake news websites, social media accounts and forged dossiers, all deployed to spread disinformation en masse.
